title: The Red Canal
subtitle: The canal behind the press enclave runs red; fishermen blame a dye unit, the unit blames the rain
coldOpen: 06:00. The canal behind the press enclave runs red.
07:00. Dead fish along two hundred metres of bank.
Fishermen gather at the dye unit’s gate.

briefing.grievance: Forty fishing families say the dye unit has been dumping at night for months and today it killed the canal. The unit says a storm drain backed up. The fish are dead either way.
knownFacts: The dye unit holds a discharge licence with a treatment plant on site.
Two hundred metres of fish kill between the unit’s outfall and the footbridge.
The pollution board’s last inspection was fourteen months ago.
unverifiedClaims: A post shows a night tanker “from the unit” emptying into the canal.
The unit says the colour comes from a holi-colour wholesaler upstream.
briefing.responsibility: You run the district pollution desk. The sample taken in the next two hours decides everything.
briefing.objective: Sample the water before it clears, find the source with evidence, and keep the gate confrontation from becoming a fire.

rightsMoments.question: A lab result proves the unit polluted the canal. Eighty people work there. What does a lawful response require?

options.text: Stop the harm now by notice, give the unit a hearing, protect the workers and the premises, and compensate those harmed from the polluter.
options.feedback: Correct. Environmental enforcement follows due process and the polluter-pays principle; it does not punish workers or skip the hearing.

options.text: Arrest the manager publicly and let the crowd decide the rest.
options.feedback: A public arrest without process turns enforcement into spectacle and endangers everyone at the gate.

options.text: Wait for the board’s monthly meeting; evidence can wait.
options.feedback: Continuing harm requires immediate interim action, which the law provides for.

rightsMoments.principle: The right to a clean environment flows from Article 21; enforcement is by lawful notice, hearing and the polluter-pays principle, with protection for the innocent at the scene.
rightsMoments.why: A sealed bottle at nine and a notice at three did what a clip and a petrol can could not.

source.label: Constitution of India, Articles 21 and 22 (India Code)

simple.question: A lab proves the factory polluted the canal. Eighty people work there. What is the lawful response?

options.a: Stop the harm now, give the factory a hearing, protect the workers, make the polluter pay.
options.b: Arrest the manager in public and let the crowd decide.

feedback.a: Yes! Stop the harm, follow the process, make the polluter pay.
feedback.b: No. A public arrest with no process is a spectacle.
feedback.c: Harm that continues needs action now.

simple.principle: A clean canal is a right. Stop the harm by notice, hold a hearing, and make the polluter pay.
simple.why: A sealed bottle at nine and a notice at three beat a clip and a petrol can.

closing.good: Two sealed bottles, a Friday hearing, and a monthly inspection that did not exist yesterday: the canal will take a season, the case will not.

closing.poor: The canal went pink before anyone filled a bottle, and the night ended with a gate on fire or a crowd charged.
